title: How plants make food: exercises
subtitle: Five exercises on the text
label: Exercises
review: Written by Claude from the lesson text. Check the English and the answers before using it with learners.

items.q: Plants eat like people and animals.
Roots take in water from the soil.
Plants take in a gas called oxygen from the air to make food.
The food that plants make is sugar.
Plants release oxygen into the soil.
What do leaves catch during the day?
How does carbon dioxide get into the plant?
options: Through tiny openings in the leaves
items.why: “Tiny openings in the leaves let this gas come in.”

items.q: What food does the plant make?
items.why: “Then the plant makes sugar, which is its food.”

items.q: What else do plants make when they make food?
items.why: “When plants make food, they also make oxygen.”

blocks.title: 4. Open questions
blocks.note: These questions are open. Talk about your answers with your teacher or a classmate.

items.q: Without looking at the text, sum it up in three sentences.
items.model: Plants make their own food. They use sunlight, water, nutrients and carbon dioxide to make sugar. This is called photosynthesis, and it also makes oxygen.

items.q: Where do plants get water and nutrients?
items.model: From the soil. Their roots take them in.

items.q: What four things do plants need to make food?
items.model: Sunlight, water, nutrients and carbon dioxide.

items.q: How do plants help people and animals?
items.model: They release oxygen into the air, and people and animals need oxygen to breathe.

items.q: Do you have plants at home or at school? What do you do to help them grow?

blocks.title: 5. Put in order
blocks.intro: Put the ideas in the order of the text.
items: Roots take in water and nutrients from the soil
Carbon dioxide comes in through tiny openings in the leaves
The plant releases oxygen into the air
